::: {.hero-meta}
10,000 customers · 20.4% annual churn · 800 calls per campaign · Databricks
:::

## The question

A bank loses one customer in five every year and has budget to call 800 of them
before they go. The question is not *who will leave* — nobody decides that. It is
**who to call with the calls you have**.

That constraint changes the problem. Recovering a customer is worth 145 €;
bothering one who was staying costs 35 €. From those two numbers a threshold
falls out:

$$p^* = \frac{35}{145 + 35} = 0.194$$

Below that probability, calling destroys value. But with fixed capacity the
threshold that actually applies is not the profitable one — it is the one the
quota imposes. The 800 highest-risk customers go in, and the cut lands at 0.73.

**Capacity turns classification into ranking.** Everything else on this site
follows from that sentence: the metric, the rival to beat, and the ceiling the
project could not cross.

::: {.thread}
The model is not judged against random guessing. It is judged against the rule
the bank could apply tomorrow with no model at all.
:::

## What came out

```{python}
#| output: asis
# .style would need jinja2, which is one more thing that has to be installed
# wherever the site is rendered. to_markdown keeps the dependency list shorter.
import charts, pandas as pd
m = charts.load("model_metrics").iloc[0]
c = charts.load("model_comparison").set_index("model")

tabla = pd.DataFrame({
    "Model":         [f"{c.loc['random_forest_tuned','average_precision']:.4f}",
                      f"{m.roc_auc:.4f}", f"{m.precision:.1%}",
                      f"{int(m.tp)} of {int(m.tp + m.fn)}"],
    "Business rule": [f"{c.loc['baseline_business','average_precision']:.4f}",
                      f"{c.loc['baseline_business','roc_auc']:.4f}", "—", "—"],
}, index=["Average precision", "ROC-AUC",
          "Precision at the operating threshold", "Churners caught in the quota"])

print(tabla.to_markdown())
```

## How it was built

Eight notebooks running from a local machine against Databricks through
Databricks Connect: **Lakebase** (Postgres 17) for the operational side,
**Unity Catalog** and **Delta** for the analytical side, **MLflow** for tracking
and the model registry, and a **Streamlit** dashboard for the retention team.

::: {.note}
The dataset is synthetic, and the project proves it rather than assuming it —
four independent signs, none of them looked for on purpose. That places a ceiling
on what any model can learn here, and the ceiling is stated instead of hidden.
:::
